cards.text: Psalm 111 opens with one word: "Hallelujah!" No warm-up, no clearing his throat, the writer comes in HOT. He's going to thank the LORD with all his heart, and he's already picked out the spot.

cards.question: The psalmist is ready to give thanks to the LORD with all his heart. Where's he going to do it?

answers.text: Among the upright in the assembly

cards.text: Then he gets to the why. The works of the LORD are great, and the folks who love those works don't just glance at them and keep scrolling.

cards.question: The great works of the LORD are ___ by all who delight in them.

cards.text: The psalmist calls God's work splendid and majestic. Me? My most majestic work ever was one cookie that came out perfectly round, and I STILL point at it with my mustache every single morning.

cards.question: Right alongside God's splendid and majestic work, the psalmist mentions His righteousness. How long does it endure?

cards.text: Take it from a stamper who spent years in the back of a junk drawer: people FORGET things. But the LORD makes sure His wonders don't end up where I did.

cards.question: True or false: the psalmist says the LORD has kept His wonders hidden away.

cards.text: Then the psalmist tells you what the LORD is like: "the LORD is gracious and compassionate." And he's not done listing yet.

cards.question: The psalmist keeps going. He says the LORD provides ___ for those who fear Him.
True or false: the psalmist says the LORD remembers His covenant forever.

cards.text: Then the psalmist brings receipts. Not a rumor, not a screenshot from somebody's group chat: God has SHOWN His people the power of His works.

cards.question: According to the psalmist, how did the LORD show His people the power of His works?

answers.text: By giving them the inheritance of the nations
By making their army larger than any other
By sending fire down on all their enemies

cards.text: The works of His hands are truth and justice. Then the psalmist moves from what God does to what God says: His precepts.

cards.question: The psalmist turns from the LORD's works to His precepts. He says all His precepts are ___.
True or false: the psalmist says the LORD's precepts hold for a while and then get replaced.

cards.text: They're upheld forever and ever, enacted in truth and uprightness. Meanwhile, the coupon I shared a junk drawer with expired YEARS ago, and it STILL believes in itself.
Then comes the big one. The psalmist slows down and tells you what the LORD has sent to His people.

cards.question: The psalmist tells what the LORD did for His people: He has sent ___ to His people.
True or false: the psalmist says the LORD has ordained His covenant for only a short time.

cards.text: He calls the LORD's name "holy and awesome." Now the psalmist lands the plane, and after all those great works and trustworthy precepts, he tells you where wisdom starts.

cards.question: According to the psalmist, what is the beginning of wisdom?
True or false: the psalmist says all who follow the LORD's precepts gain rich understanding.

cards.text: He opened with Hallelujah, and he closes with praise too: "His praise endures forever!" Me? I finish my songs by humming because I forgot the words.

findings.problem: Stop 2, card 10 quotes "holy and awesome.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: "Then he gets to the why" presents verse 2 as the reason for the thanks in verse 1. The psalm never links the two with a 'because'. It just moves from one line to the next.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: The story card says the LORD makes sure His wonders don't end up forgotten. That gives away the answer to card 8 (true or false: the LORD has kept His wonders hidden away).

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: No card sets up verse 5. Card 9 covers verse 4 and only says the psalmist is 'not done listing'. The blank asks the baker to guess the wording ('food' vs 'silver' vs 'rest'), the same kind of detail-guess as the Psalm 23 bad example.

rule.text: Never ask the baker to guess the next words of a line.

findings.problem: The right answer 'By giving them the inheritance of the nations' uses the passage's own Bible-sounding wording. The wrong answers are plain modern phrasing, so the right answer stands out.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.

findings.problem: Saying the coupon 'STILL believes in itself' claims Papa Dorin knows how his drawer friends are doing now. The backstory says he doesn't know what happened to any of them.

rule.text: His own world isn't Bible fact. His backstory, family, bakery and mission are the Dorinverse story in this file. He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them.

findings.problem: 'The psalmist slows down' says something about the text that isn't true. Verse 9 keeps the same short-line pace as the rest of the psalm.

rule.text: Noticing: What he points out must be true.

findings.problem: 'According to the psalmist, what is the beginning of wisdom?' reads like a test question, not Papa Dorin pausing mid-passage.

rule.text: Ask from inside the passage, the way a storyteller pauses to let the listener lean in.
